talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit.oak_scholar.0: Mind the roots. I'm counting this oak's rings from the inside, and she's older than any town. Take this.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit.oak_scholar.1: A visitor! The wood has been quiet. I read in here, out of the rain. A scroll, for the walk.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit.oak_scholar.2: Sit if you like. The oak keeps her own hours and I keep mine. Have this.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit.oak_retreat.0: You found my hollow. I left the courts to hear leaves instead of petitions. Take this, and tell no one.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit.oak_retreat.1: Not many come this deep. The oak doesn't mind guests, and neither do I. A scroll, for the road.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit.oak_retreat.2: Quiet here, isn't it? Only the wind arguing with the branches. Something for your trouble.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit.oak_warden.0: Careful at the roots. I look after this old oak, and she looks after me. Take this.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit.oak_warden.1: Welcome. I keep the wood's count: every fall, every sapling. A scroll, for the way back.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit.oak_warden.2: You walked softly. Good. The oak likes that. Have this.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit.oak_exile.0: I was a court wizard, once. They sent me out to the far trees. It's good to see a face. Have this.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit.oak_exile.1: A king's word put me in this oak, and no word has taken me out. A scroll, for your trouble.
talk.jaymoskingdoms.hermit.oak_exile.2: An exile's table is mostly mushrooms, but take this. I've time to write them.
dialogue.chat.jaymoskingdoms.hermit_oak_: Every ring is a year, %1$s, and some years are thin. I note which. Nobody has asked me why.
The books on the lower shelf are damp and the top shelf is dry. I read the dry ones twice.
The hollow was here before I was. I only put in a floor. Something else made the room.
I came for one winter's reading. The oak was warm, so I stayed. That was a good many winters ago.
Kings kept asking me for weather. Out here the weather simply arrives, and nobody blames me.
I pick mushrooms, I read, I mend my robe. It's a better life than the court's, %1$s.
A crow comes by some days. We don't talk. It's the best company I've had.
Folk think a hermit hates people. I only hate being asked for things. Present company excepted.
She drops her acorns every autumn, and I carry the best ones out to the clearings. The wood does the rest.
When a tree falls in my wood, I sit with it a night. Someone should.
Leave the dead branches where they lie, %1$s. The beetles have plans for them.
Some nights the whole oak creaks as if she were turning over. I don't ask her why.
They walked me out here and went home by another road. I counted the trees until I stopped minding.
The king thought a wood would finish me. The wood has been kinder than he ever was, %1$s.
I leave letters in the bark and the squirrels read them. They've sent no reply.
If you pass the capital, don't mention me. Or do. Let him know the oak is still standing.
